title: Standard Practices — Release of the Pre-Qualified Doubler Family for Lower Shell Impact Damage
abstract: Releases the four pre-qualified doubler sizes and the common fastener pattern for ground impact damage below the belly fairing, so that in-limit findings can be dispositioned by the operator without a repair approval request.

sections.planning_reason: Ground handling impact below the belly fairing generates roughly ninety repair approval requests a year, four out of five of them dents and scratches inside a narrow size band. Each request took between two and nine days to answer and in most cases produced the same repair. Operators were holding aircraft for a reply that could have been written in advance, and the design office was spending review capacity on routine findings.
sections.description: This bulletin releases four substantiated doubler sizes, the fastener pattern, the edge distance rule and the surface preparation for the lower shell panels below the belly fairing, together with the selection chart and the damage limits that admit the family. It also introduces the panel stencil that carries the family reference. No repair is required by this bulletin; it changes what an operator may do when a finding occurs.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Read the selection chart and the damage limits before any finding is dispositioned. When damage is found, clean and measure it, confirm it falls inside the admitted limits and select the doubler size from the chart. Apply the surface preparation and install the doubler with the pattern and edge distances given in SRM-M-51-10-11-004, using the fastener type stated there. Apply the stencil adjacent to the repair with the family reference and the date. Record the repair in the aircraft structural repair record. Damage outside the admitted limits still requires a repair approval request and must not be dispositioned against this bulletin.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to all MERIDIAN Family aircraft. Aircraft delivered from MSN M00435 carry the panel stencil from build; earlier aircraft receive it at the first repair accomplished under this family. There is no pre or post modification condition, because nothing on the aircraft changes until a repair is embodied.
sections.material_note: Doubler blanks in the four sizes, the cleat and the gusset for the two larger sizes are released as spares and stocked at the main line stations. Fasteners are standard and locally held. Nothing is returned.

type_data.compliance_time: No compliance time. The family is available from the date of this Service Bulletin.

tooling: Drill jig, doubler family, four sizes
